title: The Glory of God and the Good of Each Other
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Basis for Godly Living: The Imminence of Christ's Return
subpoints: The end of all things is at hand
Living in expectation of the consummation

outline.title: The Goal of Godly Living: The Glory of God
subpoints: Life as a doxology to God
All activities done for God's glory
Man's chief end is to glorify God

outline.title: The Source of Strength: God's Supplied Grace
subpoints: God provides the ability to serve
Obedience relies on divine provision, not human feeling

outline.title: The Practice of Godly Living: Other-Oriented Actions

summary:
This sermon explores the central command of 1 Peter 4:7-11, urging believers to live for the glory of God and the good of one another. The teaching establishes that this call to godly living is grounded in the eschatological truth that the end of all things is at hand. Because Christ is returning, Christians are to live with seriousness and watchfulness, viewing their current struggles as light and momentary afflictions in light of the coming consummation.

The purpose of this life is explicitly stated in verse 11: that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ. This aligns with the Reformed confession that man's chief end is to glorify God and enjoy Him forever. Every aspect of life, from mundane acts like eating and drinking to relational duties, is to be conducted as a doxology, declaring the glory of God.

Finally, the sermon outlines four other-oriented practices that reflect this godly living: prayer, love, hospitality, and the exercise of spiritual gifts. It emphasizes that the strength to perform these acts is not self-generated but is lavishly supplied by God. Believers are encouraged to rely on this divine grace, serving one another as good stewards of God's manifold grace, thereby ensuring that God receives the glory in all things.
